plain: Being widely known, often for something bad.

webster.text: Exposure to the public knowledge; the state of being publicly or generally known; as the notoriety of a crime.

example.quote: And as there would be a necessity for submitting each nomination to the judgment of an entire branch of the legislature, the circumstances attending an appointment, from the mode of conducting it, would naturally become matters of notoriety; and the public would be at no loss to determine what part had been performed by the different actors.
